features.text: Patient is 54 years old and female.
Patient experienced chest pain three months ago that lasted four days and resolved.
Chest pain was sharp, located behind the breastbone in the center of the chest, and not associated with waking up.
Chest pain could not be relieved by any attempts and was severe enough to prompt an ER visit.
Patient had difficulty swallowing during the chest pain episode.
Patient currently has no symptoms related to esophagitis.
Patient had no family history of cardiovascular disease, including heart attacks, angina, or strokes.
Patient does not smoke or consume alcohol.
Patient is trying to lose weight and does not have typical risk factors for GERD.
ER tests included an EKG and blood tests, which were normal and did not show cardiac issues.
ER blood tests were normal, with no specific mention of troponin or creatine kinase-MB levels.
No additional cardiac tests, such as stress testing or echocardiography, have been performed since the ER visit.
No upper endoscopy (EGD) or other tests for esophagitis or GERD have been performed yet.
Patient has opted to wait for symptoms before undergoing an EGD.
